references.phrase: maximal under inclusion among connected subsets
references.context: Order theory: inclusion-maximal element C of a partially ordered family of subsets, meaning there is no distinct family member D properly containing C; here family members must be connected subsets of X.
references.reason: Maximality in a partially ordered family is a reusable order-theoretic property and is not equivalent to being a largest member or having maximum cardinality.
references.matching_note: Distinguish maximal connected subset from a greatest connected subset, maximal element from maximum, and from an arbitrary open connected neighborhood.

references.disposition: Maximality is with respect to containing connected subsets, not maximum cardinality or an ambient openness assumption.

references.context: General topology: at a fixed point x of X, a neighborhood basis consisting of connected neighborhoods, such that for every neighborhood U of x some connected neighborhood V of x satisfies V⊆U; V need not be declared open unless the chosen convention explicitly requires it.
references.reason: A pointwise neighborhood-basis/refinement property is distinct from a global topology basis of open sets and is independently useful in local topological definitions.
references.matching_note: The earlier separate existing link to global topology basis should be audited: an open topological basis and a pointwise neighborhood fundamental system are related but not literally the same object.

references.phrase: each point possesses a fundamental system
references.disposition: The system is required to refine arbitrary neighborhoods, not a single globally connected covering.

references.context: Elementary set theory: singleton {x}, the set containing exactly the specified element x, viewed here as one connected component; its cardinality is one even when the ambient topological space is empty (then no such x exists).
references.reason: Singleton formation is an independently reusable elementary set construction; identifying singleton components must not be conflated with the discrete topology or a clopen singleton.
references.matching_note: Compare the prior set-notation candidate missing.2d4e4af6f3b83da929a6 for singleton versus unordered pair, but do not treat all singletons as open.
